subtopics.name: Upper GI disorders and GI bleeding

questions.stem: The nurse is teaching a client with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Which statement shows a need for more teaching?

options.text: "I'll raise the head of my bed on blocks."
"I'll have a snack right before I go to bed."
"I'll cut down on coffee, chocolate and peppermint."

rationale.correct: GERD: avoid lying down after meals, raise the head of the bed, avoid triggers and lose weight if needed.

perOption.a: Elevation reduces nighttime reflux.
perOption.b: Eating within 2 to 3 hours of lying down increases reflux.
perOption.c: These relax the lower esophageal sphincter.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: A client with a Helicobacter pylori ulcer is prescribed amoxicillin, clarithromycin and omeprazole. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.text: "I'll take all the medicines for the full 14 days, even if I feel better."
"I'll stop the antibiotics once the pain goes away."

rationale.correct: H. pylori therapy combines antibiotics with acid suppression; complete the full course.

perOption.a: Completing therapy eradicates H. pylori and prevents the ulcer from coming back.
perOption.b: Stopping early allows recurrence and resistance.
perOption.c: The antibiotics are needed to eliminate the infection.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach adherence to H. pylori therapy.

questions.stem: A client with a history of peptic ulcer disease suddenly has severe epigastric pain that spreads across the abdomen. The abdomen is rigid and board-like. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: Perforation: sudden severe pain, rigid abdomen, signs of shock. Keep the client NPO and notify the provider immediately.

perOption.a: Sudden severe pain with a rigid abdomen suggests perforation with peritonitis, a surgical emergency.
perOption.b: GERD causes burning, not a rigid abdomen.
perOption.c: This doesn't cause a rigid abdomen.
perOption.d: Ulcer pain doesn't cause a board-like abdomen.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: A client is vomiting coffee-ground material, with a heart rate of 120/min and a blood pressure of 88/54 mm Hg. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Insert two large-bore IV catheters and start fluids as prescribed
Schedule an endoscopy for next week

rationale.correct: Upper GI bleed: ABCs, large-bore IV access, fluids and blood, PPIs and urgent endoscopy.

perOption.a: Restoring volume treats the hypovolemic shock from bleeding.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.educationalObjective: Stabilize a client with an upper GI bleed.

questions.stem: When should a client take omeprazole for the best effect?

rationale.correct: PPIs: take before breakfast. Long-term use is linked to C. difficile, fractures and low magnesium.

perOption.a: PPIs work best when taken before the first meal of the day.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: A client is prescribed sucralfate. Which instruction should the nurse give?

options.text: "Take it on an empty stomach, and separate it from other medications by 2 hours."
"Take it with antacids at the same time."

rationale.correct: Sucralfate forms a protective barrier; take it 1 hour before meals and separate it from other drugs.

perOption.a: Sucralfate coats ulcers and can bind other drugs.
perOption.c: It is usually taken before meals and at bedtime.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: A client who had a gastrectomy has dumping syndrome. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.text: "I'll eat small meals, lower in carbohydrates and higher in protein, and avoid drinking with meals."
"I'll drink a large glass of juice with each meal."
"I'll eat three large meals a day."

rationale.correct: Dumping syndrome: small, frequent, low-carbohydrate meals, fluids between meals and lying down after eating.

perOption.a: This slows gastric emptying and prevents fluid shifts.
perOption.b: Fluids and sugar with meals worsen dumping.
perOption.c: Lying down after meals slows emptying.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach dietary management of dumping syndrome.

questions.stem: Which method best confirms initial placement of a nasogastric feeding tube before the first feeding?

options.text: Listening over the stomach while injecting air
Placing the tube end in water to look for bubbles

rationale.correct: Confirm initial placement by x-ray. At the bedside, check gastric aspirate pH (5 or less) and the external tube length.

perOption.a: An x-ray is the most reliable method to confirm initial placement.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)

questions.stem: A client is receiving a continuous tube feeding. Which action by assistive personnel requires the nurse to intervene?

options.text: Lowers the head of the bed flat to change the linens while the feeding runs
Keeps the head of the bed at 35 degrees
Reports that the client is coughing
Records the volume of the feeding infused

rationale.correct: Keep the head of the bed at 30 degrees or higher during feedings, and pause the feeding if the client must lie flat.

perOption.a: Lying flat with the feeding running increases the risk of aspiration; the feeding should be paused.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Which findings suggest a small bowel obstruction?

options.text: Vomiting, abdominal distention and high-pitched bowel sounds
Weight gain and constipation over months

rationale.correct: Bowel obstruction: distention, pain, vomiting and changing bowel sounds; managed with NG decompression and NPO status.

perOption.a: Early obstruction causes high-pitched bowel sounds above the blockage and vomiting.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: For each feature, indicate whether it is more typical of ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease.

rows.text: Continuous inflammation that starts in the rectum
Skip lesions anywhere from mouth to anus
Can be cured by removing the colon

rationale.correct: UC: continuous, colon only, mucosal, bloody. Crohn's: skip lesions, full thickness, anywhere in the GI tract, fistulas.

perOption.r1:c1: UC spreads continuously from the rectum.
perOption.r2:c1: UC is limited to the colon and rectum.
perOption.r2:c2: Crohn's can affect any part of the GI tract.
perOption.r3:c1: Bloody diarrhea is typical of UC.
perOption.r3:c2: Crohn's diarrhea is usually less bloody.
perOption.r4:c2: Inflammation through the full bowel wall causes fistulas.
perOption.r5:c1: Colectomy removes the disease in UC.
perOption.r5:c2: Crohn's can recur elsewhere after surgery.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Tell ulcerative colitis apart from Crohn's disease.

questions.stem: During a flare of inflammatory bowel disease, which diet should the nurse expect?

rationale.correct: IBD flare: low residue, adequate protein and calories, and NPO or parenteral nutrition if severe.

perOption.a: Low residue rests the bowel, while protein and calories meet healing needs.
perOption.b: Fiber can worsen diarrhea and cramping during a flare.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.educationalObjective: Plan nutrition during an IBD flare.

questions.stem: A client has recovered from an episode of acute diverticulitis. Which diet should the nurse teach for prevention?

rationale.correct: Acute diverticulitis: bowel rest and antibiotics. Prevention: a high-fiber diet with fluids.

perOption.a: Fiber softens stool and lowers pressure in the colon.
perOption.b: Low fiber is used during the acute phase only.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: A client with suspected appendicitis asks for a heating pad for abdominal pain. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Explain that heat should be avoided, and offer a cold pack if appropriate

rationale.correct: Appendicitis: avoid heat, laxatives and enemas; keep NPO and prepare for surgery.

perOption.a: Heat may increase inflammation and the risk of rupture.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: At what age should an adult at average risk begin colorectal cancer screening?

rationale.correct: Colorectal screening starts at 45 (colonoscopy every 10 years or other approved tests).

perOption.a: Current recommendations start screening for average-risk adults at 45.
perOption.b: This is too early for average risk.
perOption.d: Screening is for people without symptoms.

references: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommendations

questions.stem: A client is preparing for a colonoscopy. Which statement shows a need for more teaching?

options.text: "I'll have clear liquids the day before."
"I'll drink red gelatin and grape juice."

rationale.correct: Colonoscopy prep: clear liquids, no red or purple dyes, complete bowel prep, a ride home.

perOption.a: This is correct.
perOption.b: Red and purple liquids can look like blood in the colon.
perOption.c: A complete prep allows a clear view.

Slightly swollen in the first days after surgery

rationale.correct: A healthy stoma is moist and red-pink; a dusky or black stoma needs immediate attention.

options.text: Drink plenty of fluids and watch for signs of dehydration

rationale.correct: Ileostomy: high risk of fluid and electrolyte loss; chew food well and watch for blockage.

perOption.a: Ileostomy output is liquid and contains electrolytes; dehydration is a major risk.

perOption.a: This protects the skin without squeezing the stoma.
perOption.c: Too much skin is exposed to stool.

Ignore the urge to have a bowel movement

rationale.correct: Prevent constipation with fiber, fluids, activity and responding promptly to the urge.

perOption.a: These promote regular bowel movements.

questions.stem: A client is starting long-term oxycodone. Which bowel regimen should the nurse anticipate?

options.text: A stool softener with a stimulant laxative, started with the opioid
A bulk-forming laxative alone with limited fluids

rationale.correct: Opioid-induced constipation doesn't resolve with time; start a preventive regimen.

perOption.a: Opioids slow bowel movement; preventive treatment is needed.
perOption.b: Bulk without enough fluid can cause impaction.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

perOption.a: Ondansetron can prolong the QT interval and cause dysrhythmias.

questions.stem: On the second day after abdominal surgery, the client has a distended abdomen, no bowel sounds and no flatus. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: Paralytic ileus: NPO, NG decompression if needed, early walking and electrolyte correction.

perOption.a: Reduced peristalsis after surgery causes absent bowel sounds and distention.
perOption.b: Absent bowel sounds with distention isn't expected by day 2.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

rationale.correct: Rate = 1,440 mL ÷ 24 hr = 60 mL/hr.

questions.stem: The nurse is inserting a nasogastric tube. Place the steps in order.

items.text: Measure the tube from the tip of the nose to the earlobe to the xiphoid process
Confirm placement before using the tube
Insert the tube through the nostril with the head tilted slightly back
Have the client tilt the head forward and swallow as the tube is advanced
Lubricate the tip of the tube

rationale.correct: Measure, lubricate, insert, flex and swallow, confirm placement.

perOption.a: Measuring sets how far to insert the tube.
perOption.b: Lubrication makes insertion easier and reduces trauma.
perOption.c: This follows the natural curve of the nasopharynx.
perOption.d: Flexing the neck and swallowing help guide the tube into the esophagus.
perOption.e: Placement must be verified to prevent aspiration.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.
